subject.title: refactor: remove browser and codex dead exports

question: Is the current contract audit and runtime evidence sufficient to remove this broad set of browser and Codex exports without breaking a supported integration?
rationale: Repository policy requires direct sibling Codex inspection and external-contract proof before a Codex verdict, while the available evidence establishes repository-local tests but not the complete dependency or real-runtime contract.

options.title: Require complete contract proof
options.body: Rebase, cite the exact sibling Codex and package-export surfaces inspected, and provide redacted real-runtime browser and Codex smoke output before merge.

options.title: Narrow the cleanup
options.body: Land only file-private removals with unambiguous ownership and move API-shaped or weakly covered removals into focused follow-up PRs.

options.title: Accept the residual risk
options.body: Merge the complete cleanup while explicitly owning the possibility that undocumented deep imports or deleted test seams were relied upon.

recommendation.title: Require complete contract proof
recommendation.body: Rebase, cite the exact sibling Codex and package-export surfaces inspected, and provide redacted real-runtime browser and Codex smoke output before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the merged export ratchet and has the strongest recent history across the affected cleanup surfaces.
